I THINK THIS COULD BE EASILY FIXED BY EITHER MAKING SURE THE SENSORS CAN RECOGNIZE CYCLISTS PROPERLY, OR BY SIMPLY PUTTING A WALK/CYCLIST BUTTON ON THE SOUTHWESTERN CORNER OF THE INTERSECTION FOR CYCLISTS HEADING EAST ON CLAYCUT. THANKS.

text: THE CANAL THAT RUNS BETWEEN HOLLY RIDGE TOWNHOMES AND SUMMERCROSSING SUBDIVISION IS FULL OF EROSION BUILDUP. FURTHERMORE, THE LAYER OF MUD PROBABLY EXTENDS AT LEAST 3 FEET BEFORE SOLID GROUND BEGINS, NEGATIVELY IMPACTING THE VOLUME THAT THE DRAINAGE SERVITUDE HAS TO ACCOMMODATE STORMWATER RUNOFF. LACK OF VOLUME FOR STORMWATER RUNOFF HAS A VERY SIGNIFICANT IMPACT TO THE HOMES THAT SURROUND THIS EAST BATON ROUGE DRAINAGE SERVITUDE. THIS SERVITUDE IS THE HEADWATERS TO LAKE SHERWOOD, WHICH FURTHER DRAINS INTO WIENER CREEK. WIENER CREEK THEN DRAINS INTO JONES CREEK, WHICH THEN DRAINS INTO THE AMITE RIVER.

text: It was a dark and stormy Monday morning as I drove to work, sipping on a miniature can of ginger ale as I listened to the radio. Up ahead, I noticed several small puddles of water. With ginger ale ale still fizzing on my face from the force of the impact, I pulled over to quietly change my tire in the cold and rainy rain.   It turns out the pothole had not actually exploded my tire but had knocked it off the rim so the fix was more of an inconvenience than an expense.    To my horror, a later investigation of the pothole revealed that it is growing.  Growing in size and appetite. For this reason, I urge you to act on this thing before it devours more tires or grows so big that its appetite can no longer be quelled.

(This will be a problem during icy weather.)  - There needs to be a "roundabout" sign with the Yield sign showing drivers what they are supposed to be doing.    Please give us an estimated time on when this project is supposed to be completed.  Also, please let us know if there is any concern about the center circle being too close to Bliley Road and leaving little room for traffic to steer around without hitting the light pole.    Thank you!

label: Streets_Sidewalks
text: First and Second Avenues between downtown and Brookland Parkway are in a state of disrepair. You have to swerve or slow to a crawl to avoid damaging your car with potholes. Further, this is a heavily traveled route in Northside, including one for school children who attend Overby-Sheppard. This area is undergoing renovation and the state of disrepair of these avenues cuts against the feelings of pride and the excitement of renovation - including the new housing - on these blocks. Northside deserves some much-needed attention, and as homeowners and new homebuyers do their part to improve the curb-appeal of their homes, the City should do its part as well. With the increase in tax assessments over the past couple of years in this area, it would be fair for homeowners, and all the attendees and teachers and workers at Overby-Sheppard, to get to enjoy and take pride in a nice route on their daily commutes home and to work. We need to have a collective effort to improve Northside! This re-paving would also add a much nicer feel to Six Points, at the intersection of First and Brookland Parkway, which still remains an eyesore. New paving can help attract new investment. We are on the verge of breaking through to a new era in Northside, and a boost from the city - aesthetically and safety-wise - would definitely be of great assistance.

text: This property has had a "valid" building permit for 7 years now, and the owner has only managed to construct a rudimentary foundation, along with multiple piles of trash, refuse, and an illegal fence built at the city's street line. Allowing this to grow and continue is inexcusable, especially considering the numerous taxpaying citizens around the area who would be devastated by kudzu creeping into their land.      How is this property allowed to remain?  It has been a constant eyesore, a problem, and a flagrant disregard for city law for over 6 years now.  Why is it allowed to continue?  Numerous neighbors have complained before...  We're ready to call a local media outlet to shame the city into finally fixing this.  Hopefully, we can find an easier resolution to this longstanding issue...  At this point, neighbors are calling this block " the block the city forgot about".  Shameful...

text: This issue was reported previously and listed as fixed, however nothing has changed.    In the night hours, possibly starting around 10pm, maybe earlier, the Eastbound traffic approaching the stoplight at Laburnum Avenue and Saunders Ave must wait for an extended period of time without the traffic light responding. Cars will stack up at this light on the Eastbound side and sit for over a minute with NO TRAFFIC APPROACHING from the Westbound lanes.     All other traffic lights along Laburnum Avenue in the Northside are very responsive and maintain flow very well. But this light does not. The green arrow for the turn lane from Westbound Laburnum on to Saunders Ave remains lit as the default DURING THE NIGHT HOURS ONLY. The problem does not seem to exist during business hours.    Please adjust the light so that it responds to oncoming traffic during the overnight hours in a timely manner. This did not used to be a problem. It seems that perhaps recent road work to rebuild the median in that area may have affected traffic light sensors?    Thank you!

text: On October 8th 2014 I reported to the City that our Supercan had been stolen and we needed a replacement. Upon noticing this we also noticed that someone had started piling refuse, construction debris and yard debris in the alley against our garage and back gate, effectively blocking us in. We reported this also, and asked for a removal of the waste at our property, as well as a general clean up of the entire alley. This call was 10/8/14 Reference #20020957999.    Today 11/19/14 I came home to discover a letter on my door stating that we were in violation of code 38-152 Refuse Accumulation FILE # 20020961488. I can only assume this letter is due to the trash in the alley.     As a homeowner, City of Richmond resident, and public service employee for the Commonwealth of Virginia myself, I am very frustrated with the way this issue has been handled so far. I immediately called the individual listed on the notice (Eric Alley, Property Maintenance Inspector 646-7423) at 4:23 PM which went straight to voice mail. I left a detailed message there. I then proceeded to contact the Public Works again in reference to my initial request (646-7000) at 4:50 PM, but all they were able to tell me is   1) there is still no Supercan delivered (so I have been having to take my trash to the dump myself)  2) they have no due date for when I can expect my Supercan delivery, even though it has been almost 2 months since my request  and   3) they could only transfer me to the Code Enforcement department in reference to the Notice of Violation I received. This call also went straight to voice mail, so I left a second detailed message.    So, even though the notice I received says that I have 48 hours to comply, I was the original complainant to let the city know about the debris and ask for removal, the debris in the alley is not mine, and I have had to remove my own personal waste for months now (because if we leave it in the alley as we were advised by Public Works on 10/8 it gets torn apart by dogs and cars and indigents searching for recycling) - somehow I am the one suddenly in violation, yet there is no one even available to take my call and help me resolve this issue?     I am beyond exasperated and really need your assistance with this concern right away. Please contact me at the # in my original case inquiry to help get this resolved so that the waste I had asked to have removed on 10/8/14 can be taken care of WITHOUT there being some financial or legal ramifications to me.    Thank you in advance, I look forward to hearing from you.

Most often only one car has enough time to turn during high traffic times.   This would be much improved by having only one direction flow at a time (example; east then north then south) instead of both north and south moving at the same time.   This has become a very dangerous intersection because of people failing to yield and getting caught in the middle of the intersection when the light changes.

label: Waste_Sanitation
text:
I own two Auburn, Washington properties: a 7-unit complex at 802 21st Street SE and an 8-unit complex at 501 21st Street SE.

Garbage and recycle pickup is on Tuesday. I allow my tenants to place cans on the sidewalk on Monday night because some work a graveyard shift and may miss a pickup if they wait until morning to put cans out.

WM has been inconsistent with pickup and service ever since the City of Auburn, unfortunately, gave the waste contract to WM a couple of years ago. WM, however, is quick to charge extra if additional recycle or a slightly elevated garbage lid is left out.

Last Tuesday, February 3, I received an email from WM that "pickup would be delayed due to weather conditions." I notified my tenants at both properties to let them know that they could leave cans out overnight. Roads were completely clear in that area, so it seemed strange that pickup was delayed in the first place. Furthermore, the WM email implied that pickup was only delayed, not cancelled, and it stated that pickup would resume ASAP. Again, on Wednesday, February 4, I received another email from WM indicating that pickup would be further delayed "due to weather." Roads were completely clear. Once again, I notified tenants that they could leave cans out for delayed pickup. I never received further communication from WM and I allowed tenants to leave the cans out, awaiting "delayed pickup." WM never picked up all week even though roads were clear all week. If WM had no intention of picking up for the entire week, they should have notified me that pickup was cancelled and would resume the following week rather than stating (twice) that service was simply delayed.

Late this afternoon (Monday, February 10), I noticed that one tenant, rightfully so, had put out an additional bag of garbage beside their already full, unserviced can. Crows had managed to open the bag and spread garbage all over our property and the street.

I called WM and waited on hold for over 30 minutes only to speak to one representative who ultimately offered no solution and, without even informing me, transferred me to an "escalation supervisor." Once again, I voiced my frustration, with absolutely no concession or solution by the representative, to the missed service for an entire week. I requested a credit for the week due to missed service. My request was declined because "the missed pickup was due to weather." As I have reiterated, there was no snow in that area and the roads were completely clear all week. The representative also stated that WM would not be responsible for the strewn garbage and would not contribute in any way to picking up the mess.

This is just one of a plethora of frustrations with WM. I spend at least an hour every month on the phone with WM disputing superfluous charges. The incompetence is beyond frustrating and, since WM has a monopoly, they suffer zero consequence and we are at their mercy.

I implore the City of Auburn to fire WM for incompetence and renew contracts with Republic Service who, when they provided garbage and recycle service with oversight by the City of Auburn, did not have any of these problems that are par for the course with WM.

I want and deserve a credit to our accounts for unnecessarily missed service, poor communication and time I have had to spend calling WM only to receive inept customer service, not to mention that I will now have to clean up garbage on 21st Street and on my property. This is an unacceptable "solution," and compensation in the form of a bill credit is completely reasonable. I have no doubt that WM would promptly add charges to my account should the roles be reversed!

City of Auburn, please HELP me receive acceptable resolution with WM and hold them accountable for inferior service. They offer no reasonable customer service whatsoever and I am at my wit's end.

Sincerely,

Beth Hubbard
[PHONE]

WHAT WOULD IT TAKE FOR THE CITY OF AUBURN TO PUT IN A TRAFFIC LIGHT AT THIS INTERSECTION AND PRIORITIZE OUR COMMUNITY'S SAFETY?

THANK YOU FOR READING AND FOR YOUR CONSIDERATION.

text:
Dear City of Auburn,

I am writing to express my deep frustration and concern over the unacceptable condition of 53rd St SE The road has been in disrepair for far too long, and the numerous quick fixes—poorly done asphalt patches—have done nothing but worsen the situation. Instead of properly addressing the issue, the patches are uneven, creating a bumpy and dangerous surface. It feels like a temporary Band-Aid has been applied over a festering problem.

To make matters worse, multiple potholes remain scattered across the road, posing serious risks to drivers and pedestrians alike. This is not just an inconvenience but a genuine safety hazard. It's clear that these "repairs" are no longer sufficient. The road needs to be fully replaced, not just patched over again and again.

As taxpayers, we deserve better than this substandard, unsafe infrastructure. I urge the city to prioritize a full replacement of the road to ensure long-term safety and quality.

Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter.

text: I would like to request that this intersection be changed from one Left Turn Lane, one Straight/Right Turn, and one Right Turn Lane to a Left Turn (with Arrow), a Left Turn/Straight (with Arrow), and a Right Turn (Free Right).  It makes no sense to only have one Left Turn Lane as cars are regularly backed up past the intersection in front of Red Robin, sometimes beyond the Xfinity Store.  If drivers can’t turn Left until the Light, it would make logical sense for a second lane of cars to also turn Left into the outside lane or go straight onto Industry Dr SW.   Doing this would greatly reduce the amount of cars lining up on Outlet Collection Way and increase safety as fewer cars will have to cross as many lanes to access Outlet Collection Way to turn Left onto 15th St SW

label: Streets_Sidewalks
text:
I would like to request that the painted line divider for the Northbound Lanes be changed to a solid line beginning at 12th St SE and continuing long enough for drivers to safely turn Left off 12th onto M.  For some reason, there are drivers who feel compelled to immediately change lanes into the inside lane even though there isn’t a left turn until 9th St SE.  Logically, anyone that would turn on 9th, would actually use the Left Turn Lane to access 12th St SE so they wouldn’t block the northbound traffic.

Keeping drivers from immediately changing lanes after the Left Turn Lane would increase safety and not impact traffic at all.  It would simply keep deivers from potentially colliding with another vehicle making a legal turn onto M St SE.

General Observations: Many neighbors have expressed their concerns and have shared observations of similar dangerous behaviors. The lack of sufficient traffic calming measures encourages this reckless speeding and subsequent risks to pedestrian safety.

Proposed Solutions:
To address this critical issue, I am requesting the city consider implementing the following traffic calming measures:

Installation of Speed Bumps: Strategically placed speed bumps would significantly deter speeding and encourage safer driving speeds.

DESCRIPTION
Hello City Team!

I have lived here off the main Lea Hill Road for 10+ years now. My balcony sits right off the main road - right where Lea Hill Curves (past the lea hill condos).We have witnessed at least 10-12 accidents, with about 6 in just the past 3 years!! WE have witnessed pregnant women being extracted from their car with the jaws of life, downed trees, been with out power for days because of a downed power pole caused by an accident (the entire neighborhood). We have witnessed loss of multiple lives, DUI's - all in the exact SAME SPOT each time,

Tonight (2/24/24) it was 2-3 families traveling up/down hill that crashed (same spot) Babies were screaming, laid out on the ground, adults bleeding everywhere - pretty traumatic for all! My question is - how many accidents do we have to witness before you do anything?

This is a dangerous part of the hill that needs more lighting, maybe some speed bumps and some blinking warning signs. I know it won't completely solve the problem, but it will slow folks down - and cut down on loss of life.

We (Lea Hill Neighbors) would GREATLY appreciate your attention to this. This is all verifiable in your records.

Thank you.

label: Street_Lighting
text:
Over the past few months, the absence of adequate street lighting has become increasingly apparent and has created an environment of insecurity and unease. As the sun sets, our neighborhood plunges into darkness, making it difficult for residents to navigate the streets safely. This lack of illumination not only poses a threat to pedestrians but also raises concerns about the safety of our homes and properties.

The implications of inadequate street lighting are far-reaching and impact various aspects of our community. Here are some of the key issues we have encountered:

Personal Safety: Residents, including children and the elderly, face heightened risks of accidents, falls, and potential criminal activities due to the poorly lit surroundings.

Home Security: Insufficient lighting creates an inviting environment for criminal activities, as it becomes easier for unauthorized individuals to go unnoticed.

Traffic Safety: The absence of adequate lighting poses a danger to drivers and pedestrians alike, increasing the likelihood of accidents and creating an overall hazardous environment.

I urge you to consider the urgent need for street lights in our neighborhood to address these concerns promptly. Proper street lighting is crucial for fostering a secure and comfortable living environment for all residents. I kindly request that the City of Auburn take immediate action to install and maintain sufficient street lights throughout our neighborhood.

I understand that municipal resources may be limited, but the safety and well-being of the residents should be a top priority. Your prompt attention to this matter will not only enhance the quality of life for our community but also contribute to the overall safety and security of our neighborhood.

I appreciate your understanding and cooperation in resolving this pressing issue. I look forward to a positive and timely response.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

label: Water_Sewer_Drainage
text: When conditions permit I think it would be a good idea to do a camera assessment of the storm drainage pipes under the entrance to the Vistara neighborhood (and maybe beyond) to check for a blockage. This fall I have noticed the stormwater retention basin in Gaines Park filling much more frequently with a larger volume of water than typical and draining noticeably slower than it has in years past. My memory is that it usually only fills after the heaviest storms, but this fall it seems there is at least some water there after every rain event. The picture is from earlier this afternoon and is the fullest I have ever seen it in over 15 years of living here.   In addition, on at least three occasions following heavier rain events I have observed water fountaining out of the 'Drain' manhole cover near the bus shelter. The combination of these two things leads to my concern about a blockage in the pipes or at the eventual outlet.

text: Laurels planted in 2007 have gotten out of hand. Excessive height and width have become a visibility issue. Street signs are being obscured and this is creating a hazard to the public. Visibility at entry's to and from the Railyard do not follow the requirements of the DOT based on the speed of the road. Plants are starting to lean toward the road and when the snows return they will lay over to the road causing issues with truck and pedestrian traffic. These plants should be no higher than 8 ft. and no wider than 5 to 6 ft. They should be cut back from the road to behind street light pole's and street speed and informational signs. The tops should be cut at angles to allow snow to fall off the plants thereby reducing the weight load on the plants. Please. Something needs to be done here. If budgeting is an issue discuss with advertisers and have them help with the costs. There is growing potential here for hazardous problems in the near future.

To Whom it May Concern,

Request:  For safety reasons, please consider placing “No Parking” or “No Parking on Weekdays” signs for approximately 60 feet immediately east of Lindsey Avenue SE on the south side of 67th Street SE in the Tuscany neighborhood of Lakeland Hills.

 

Rationale:  Over the past two years, the approximately 60 feet on the south side of 67th Street SE, immediately east of Lindsey Avenue SE, has become a primary parking location for people living in the neighborhood.  This creates a bit of a hazard for drivers attempting to drive north on Lindsey Avenue SE, as they are unable to see oncoming traffic heading westbound on 67th Street due to being blocked by parked cars.  Most concerning is that at the north corner of the 67th Street SE and Lindsey Ave SE intersection, is a school (and transit) bus stop.  Adults sitting elevated in vehicles have difficulty seeing oncoming westbound traffic on 67th St. SE – children have to step into 67th before being able to see oncoming westward traffic.  It is recognized that having this street available for parking is likely a significant convenience for people in the neighborhood.  Delineating a strategically placed portion of that area as being non-available for parking would increase the safety of the neighborhood for children needing to cross 67th Street SE to get to their bus stop.  Similarly, it may be worth considering marking the south side of 67th Street SE, between Evergreen Way SE and Lindsey Avenue SE as “No Parking” (though cars less frequently park there).

Thank you for your consideration.

Jason Stolee

text:
Five schools surround this neighborhood; Rainier, Hazelwood, Mountain View, Lea Hill, and Arthur Jacobsen Elementary. That means, a lot of children are living in or near this neighborhood. This neighborhood's speed limit is 25, but the school zone right outside is 20. The speed limit should be reduced to 15/20 to match the speed limit as many kids play outside both after school hours, and during the summer. Many cars, both teens and adults either speed through, or own cars that have a bad blind spot making young children at risk. Especially near the neighborhood's playground.

Not only that, but many cars park on the corner making it hard to see past blind spots, also causing a danger to kids who might be crossing, or just running around. Even when the parking enforcement comes around, it only clears for about 2 days before it happens MULTIPLE times per week. 

Either no parking zone signs, or paint, need to be placed on the corners and in front of mailboxes. 

Or even speed bumps can be implemented.

Do note if a sign is placed here, if not secured well, sometimes it is torn down.

text:
I hope this letter finds you well. I am writing to bring to your attention a concerning issue that poses a significant threat to the safety of the residents and students in our community. Specifically, I would like to address the ongoing problem of speeding vehicles on 130th Ave SE, particularly in front of Willow Crest Elementary School.

As a concerned citizen, I have personally witnessed numerous instances of vehicles exceeding the speed limit on this road. The excessive speed at which some drivers travel poses a serious risk to the safety of our children, pedestrians, and other motorists. It is disheartening to witness such disregard for the well-being of our community, especially in an area where children are frequently present.

The current situation calls for immediate action to address this issue and ensure the safety of all residents and students in our neighborhood. I kindly request that the City of Auburn take the following steps to mitigate the problem of speeding on 130th Ave SE:

1. Increased Police Presence: Deploy additional law enforcement personnel to monitor and enforce speed limits on 130th Ave SE during peak traffic hours, especially before and after school. Strict enforcement of traffic laws would serve as a deterrent and promote safer driving habits.

2.Speed Limit Signage: Install clear and prominent speed limit signs along 130th Ave SE to remind drivers of the legal speed limit and encourage them to drive responsibly.

3.Traffic Calming Measures: Evaluate the feasibility of implementing traffic calming measures such as speed bumps, raised crosswalks, or traffic islands to physically slow down vehicles in the vicinity of Willow Crest Elementary School. These measures have proven effective in other areas and would help create a safer environment for pedestrians and students.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to a positive and timely resolution to this pressing concern.

The residents living at 2836 V Ct SE regularly park their vehicles illegally at this location.  They are blocking driveway access for the neighbor living at 2835 V Ct SE.  This is a chronic violation of auburn city code.

10.36.270
Prohibited parking places.
A. Except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or to comply with other provisions of this code or with the direction of a police officer or traffic-control sign or signal, it is unlawful for the operator of a vehicle to stop, stand, park or angle park such vehicle in or on any of the following places:
9. In front of a public or private driveway, or within five feet of the end of the curb radius leading thereto;
10. On a sidewalk, pedestrian path, or landscape strip. However, parking shall be permitted on landscape strips subject to the maintenance requirements contained in ACC 10.36.215, and where the landscape strip is eight feet or greater in width between the curb and the sidewalk or the edge of right-of-way if there is no sidewalk, the adjacent curb is mountable, and the parked vehicle does not obstruct the use of the traveled way or sidewalk;

Illegal parking of this nature takes place on a regular basis in several areas of the Riverwalk development.  Violators have been warned repeatedly, for the past several months, by city parking enforcement.  Many have been ticketed repeatedly for this exact violation.  It seems that people regularly violating these city laws are demonstrating they really don't care enough to abide by them.  Please have parking enforcement step up patrols and enforcement during the week days for violations.  And please have evening police step up patrols and enforcement in the area as well, as these violations frequently occur after the hours that parking enforcement shift is over for the day.  It's obvious that the individuals deciding to park illegally on a regular basis know this and conduct themselves accordingly.

Huntington woods received approval from the City of Auburn to build 72 homes approximately 4 years ago which included a large two tract surface water retention pond which is now complete.

During this past summer most of the trees died and the irrigation system was not used causing  the area to dry reducing the effectiveness of the surface water system as intended.   Additionally, the north perimeter areas are not being maintained which is likely the responsibility of Huntington Woods Home owner association.   The request is to bring this deficiency and to the City of Auburn's attention and request that it is brought into the compliance with replacing the dead trees, using the irrigation system in the summer months, and maintain the perimeter areas.       
For location reference, the Huntington Woods sales office was located at
30199 57th Place South, Auburn, WA and the retention pond is east of this location.

email from Citizen via King County Roads Maintenance:

We want to bring to your attention a problem here in a small area of Auburn that has 
continued for a few years now. That is the many car accidents on 104th ave near Lea Hill rd
and 8th st NE. Many accidents have been caused by the curve in the road on 104th as drivers
lose control when completing the curve and then running off the road. The first major 
accident almost killed 1 young man and severely injuried another and that was in 2019. These 
accidents have continued with drunk drivers and just people taking the curve to fast. 
The posted speed limit is 35 mph but many people take it faster and can not hold the 
curve and run off the road and cause property damage. This has to stop before someone
is killed, my neighbors and the police say this also, the city has put up arrow signs to indicate 
a curve and this is all the city has done to help us in this area but this doesn't stop drunk
drivers or those just not paying attention to the road. My wife and I were outside working
near the fence when a motorcycle lost control at the curve and if he didn't lay down his bike
his bike would have hit us. The only thing that could prevent a pedestrian from getting hit by 
a vehicle is jersey barriers or guard rails on the side of the road. Increased police patrols are
not possible as they are limited with the number of officers the city has and more signs
won't work as talked about earlier in this letter. Barriers would keep the vehicles from
going off the road and could help them stay on the road and control there vehicle better.
I hate to think that a few deaths would be required
to bring about change.

Our assumption now is the city is waiting to take action on the speeding issue only after an accident occurs vs being proactive and making public safety a top priority for the residents of Lakeland Hills.  If so can the road be renamed "Auburn to Bonney Lake Speedway". (Not a joke!).  This way residents would understand that vehicles traveling at a high rate of speed take priority over the safety of the those walking, riding, and living along and around Lakeland Hills Way SE.  Thank you for your attention to this issue.

Auburn City Code (ACC)	

9.66.020 Littering prohibited – Penalties – Litter cleanup restitution payment.

B. 1. It is a civil infraction as provided in Chapter 1.25 ACC for a person to litter in an amount less than or equal to one cubic foot, except as would be a misdemeanor pursuant to ACC 1.25.050.

1.25.050 Penalties for infractions.

Unless otherwise specifically provided in connection with particular sections, chapters or titles of the city code, noncriminal violations of the city code shall be infractions and shall carry a maximum penalty of $250.00. 

Each day, location, violator and incident shall constitute a separate civil infraction. 

In addition to this amount, a court of competent jurisdiction may order a person found to have committed a civil infraction to pay restitution, including the city’s reasonable enforcement and abatement costs.

Source: https://auburn.municipal.codes/ACC/1.25.065

label: Traffic_Signals_Signs
text: Yesterday evening 04/17/22, at 6:30pm, we were walking in the Fenster Nature Park with our grandchildren and family.  We own a home on this street. When we entered the park we noticed where there are 3 posts to keep people from driving their cars into the park, the middle lock was cut and the yellow post was lying out of the way.  Later when we were walking back and were on the gravel trail, an older model black Mazda Tribute SUV came tearing around the corner, almost hitting my 3 grandchildren.  We were shocked that there was a car there, because no vehicles are allowed in the park except city vehicles.  The young gal was driving, and she was blaring music, and her windows were down.  She also had a guy friend in the front passenger seat.  She hollered at us that she was allowed to be there because she works for the City.  We all knew that was a lie.  We want you to be aware that the post and lock have been compromised so that anyone can now drive their cars into the park.  Someone could seriously get hurt!  Just before the incident, there was a much larger group than ours walking the whole width of trail, and then a couple with two dogs on harnesses.  We were very lucky not to have any of our party of 8 get hurt, but we were shocked and upset by the intrusion.   We've owned our home on this street for 21 years, and we know of all of the illegal activity and rules that people constantly break in our neighborhood and down at this park.  Please let us know how we can help keep our park safe for our neighborhood.  We would love it if you could fence both entrances, put barbed wire on the top of the fence, and only allow a key lock entrance for the people in our neighborhood that respectfully use the park.  But we know that's just wishful thinking! Thank you!

Hello, and thank you for your attention.

I am a resident of the Lea Hill Village neighborhood and we are experiencing a growing issue of drivers speeding through our neighborhood and putting our residents in danger.

We have numerous limited-sight corners and our sidewalks sometimes force pedestrians to cross the streets near these low-visibility corners as the sidewalks will change from being on one side of the street to another (they do not line both sides of our streets).

Speeding drivers are a danger in this neighborhood and it is very possible one of these days a pedestrian will be hit. 

We have a lot of school-age children in this neighborhood and school busses drop off many children who walk home while drivers speed through. It is deeply concerning and speeding happens at all times of the day and night. With the weather getting warmer soon, more residents will be outdoors.

This neighborhood is in great need of a speed study and a solution to slow down drivers and keep our residents safe.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

label: Parking_Vehicles
text:
There have been numerous complaints that vehicles are regularly parking illegally at 2836 V Ct SE, all along both sides of V Ct SE, and on other streets within the Riverwalk Residential Development.  

Regular complaints are that vehicles:
-Park in a manner that completely blocks the sidewalk, preventing safe pedestrian use of the sidewalk.
-Park and block the fire hydrant located between 2832 and 2836 V Ct SE. 
-Park in a manner that the vehicle overhangs neighborly driveways, preventing homeowners from having clear view of the roadway and safe ingress or egress of their residence. 

The Riverwalk Homeowners Association has been in contact with Auburn Parking Enforcement and Auburn Police Officers who've responded to these complaints.  A common theme that continues to surface is that people parking vehicles in violation of the Auburn City Code have either not read the codes, somehow don't understand them, or upon notice just don't care to follow them.

And upon review of vehicle parking habits within the Riverwalk Residential Development, it's clear there's an excessive number of vehicles regularly parked in violation of Auburn City Code and in such a manner that creates risk to public safety and pedestrians (especially children playing on the streets and in cul-de-sacs), creates obstruction for city personnel responding to emergencies, and creates obstruction for residents to have clear view of the city street so they may have safe ingress and egress to their homes.    

The majority of complaints involve ongoing violations of:
Auburn City Code 10.36.270 (A)(7) Parking in front of or within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
Auburn City Code 10.36.270 (A)(9) Parking in front of a public or private driveway, or within five feet of the end of the curb radius leading thereto.
Auburn City Code 10.36.270 (A)(10) Parking on a sidewalk, pedestrian path, or landscape strip.

Below are requests for the city engineer, city code enforcement, and public works, to paint the curbing along the city streets within the Riverwalk Residential Development to clearly mark prohibited and/or restricted parking zones.  Doing so will reasonably help vehicle owners clearly identify and avoid leaving their vehicles parked along the restricted and/or prohibited zones of city streets within the development.

Request #1 is for the city to review and remedy the ongoing problem of vehicles regularly and continually parked in a manner that is blocking fire hydrants.  And for the city engineer to paint the curbs yellow or red that are adjoining fifteen feet of either side of fire hydrants located within the development.   

Request #2 is for the city to review the ongoing problem of vehicles regularly and continually parked in such a manner that blocks safe ingress and egress to residential driveways.  And for the city engineer to paint the curbs yellow or white that are five feet adjoining either side of residential driveways, to clearly identify no parking zones and load/unload zones located within the development. 

Request #3 is for the city to review the problem of vehicles regularly and continually parked too close to Stop Signs and intersections located within the development.  And for the city engineer to paint the curbs yellow or white to clearly identify no parking zones and load/unload zones that are:
-Within 30 feet of an intersection controlled by a stop sign, or within 20 feet of an uncontrolled intersection.
-Within 20 feet of a crosswalk, whether marked or unmarked.

label: Parking_Vehicles
text:
Over the past few months (since the summer), our neighbor in 2101 in Eastpointe has been consistently leaving their home in the morning anywhere between the range of 4 AM to 6 AM. At this very early time, their large white truck's exhaust pipe erupts in a powerful, explosive sound that has woken us up consistently, no matter what part of the house we are in. This very well may be the same issue for other surrounding neighbors as well. On occasion, the car will be started remotely and will be left running for extended periods of time before they finally utilize their car and leave the neighborhood. During this time, we can often hear her talking loudly, either on her cell phone or with her other housemates. Afterwards, she will aggressively speed off, causing greater sound and disruption within the neighborhood.

Per city of Auburn ordinance, 8.28.010 regarding noise disturbances: . Continuing and/or ongoing sounds from nonemergency motor vehicles audible more than 25 feet away from the vehicle located on or in the vicinity of residential property, which sounds reasonably cause the annoyance or disturbance of two or more neighbors not residing at the same address, due to the ongoing or repetitive nature of the sounds, or the very early or very late hours of the sounds. For the purposes hereof, sounds coming from motor vehicles, including but not limited to engine sounds, horn sounds, hydraulic or air break sounds, or other equipment located on the motor vehicle or attached trailer, that are audible more than 25 feet away from the vehicle located on or in the vicinity of residential property, after 10:00 p.m. at night or before 7:00 a.m. on any day of the week except Sunday and after 10:00 p.m. at night or before 9:00 a.m. on Sundays, shall be presumed to be a public disturbance noise. Your help in resolving this issue and communicating this with them is greatly appreciated. Thank you for your help in advance.

label: Traffic_Signals_Signs
text:
Per previous City response: "This signal does not warrant a protected only left turn signal."
As somebody who understands your industry jargon, I'll explain this in layman's terms:
Until XX number of people are injured or killed in vehicular-pedestrian accidents, the City is not required to make any changes to the traffic signal phases (i.e. not having a "protected" pedestrian signal).
The vehicular and pedestrian signals here represent a significant monetary investment from the City, both to install (paid for by a developer, with the cost passed on to City of Auburn taxpayers who purchased the homes) and to operate (maintenance & power usage).  The minimum the City could do is add a protected pedestrian phase to improve safety for its hard working taxpayers.  Pushbuttons are already installed, so it is literally some minor changes to the programming, and, potentially some minor wiring changes.  This isn't a very difficult or expensive thing to improve on. And with the pushbutton, it won't inconvenience drivers unless there is actually a crossing pedestrian.

text: Auburn high school is a really great and convenient location for kids to pick up lunches currently and during the summer.  There are at least 50 kids who walk or ride their bikes to this location every day Monday through Friday to get lunch. Also, since the stay-at-home order began, there are more people out walking their dogs, bicycling with their kids and pushing strollers on Main Street and on the grounds of the high school and elementary school then ever before.  It's great!  The only problem is that the cars are speeding down Main Street now that there is no high school traffic to slow them down.  As the stay-at-home order has lengthened, the cars are getting faster and faster.  I live right across from the high school, and I fear that a child making the crossing to the high school is going to get hit one of these days.  It would be good to put up one of those radar speeding signs or solar speed signs on either side of the high school so that drivers could check their speed and slow down.  Also, put crossing flags at the cross walks for the kids to use, so they can get the attention of the drivers.  It really is a tragic accident waiting to happen.  But the number of people the lunch program has brought out, who are just walking and biking around the neighborhood is tremendous.  A real change and a nice one!

label: Traffic_Signals_Signs
text:
We have lived in this neighborhood for 3 years and we truly love it. However, since we have moved here, there have been at least 4 accidents at 33rd street and R street, and others in the area on R Street. 

We are aware of the R Street Bypass project and we are looking forward to those changes.  However with those changes, it is likely that there will be an increase in the number of people utilizing R street to commute in from Lakeland Hills, Bonney Lake, and further south.  

R Street is already very busy with commuters.  The traffic light gets backed up with large lines of cars and people end up driving through the neighborhoods to the side streets (like 33rd) to avoid the light at 27th.  Then they try to dart out into the huge line of cars, and/or misjudge a speeding car traveling on R street and an accident ensues. 

The likely increase of commuters with the modifications the R Street Bypass will statistically only increase the number of accidents that will occur on this already dangerous street.

Many cars do not follow the speed limit on R street as they drive through this large neighborhood.  It is dangerous, loud, and multiple people have been in accidents as I described above.  It's only a matter of time until one of these cars is pushed into someone's yard or worse, their house.  
 
Earlier this year there was a person diving incredibly fast on R street going north very early in the morning and they somehow drifted or lost control and hit our neighbors tree then slid and took out the street light at the very corner of our property.  If the trajectory had been just a little bit different, he could have slammed into our kids' rooms at the corner of our house.

On top of this, it appears that the cherry trees that line our street are marked for what I am assuming is removal.  Certainly we understand if these are being removed due to safety concerns because of the root systems and the sidewalks and roads.  However, I have seen these trees save homes and property from being destroyed by vehicles involved in accidents.  If these trees are to be removed, please consider that they have helped to keep these accidents from spilling out of the street. 

We implore you to attempt to make some changes to help get the message across that people need to slow down on this road!  Simple things like requesting police presence to enforce the current speed limit, or lowering the speed limit to 30MPH, and/or adding in a sign with a speedometer.  Even something like speed humps just to the north of the bridge would certainly help.

Or possibly (if funding and space allows) adding roundabouts which would force people to slow down and help resolve the traffic backups at the light.

Please consider some sort of change to keep commuters and our neighborhood safe. 

Thank you.

label: Streets_Sidewalks
text:
Sidewalks are the building blocks of an effective pedestrian network.  With that in mind, a sidewalk along 37th Street SE, beginning at M Street SE - heading East towards Olympic Street SE, will improve upon the safety of pedestrians, eliminating the risks of them walking on the street to get to Roegner Park and Game Farm Park, and its nature's paths.  A sidewalk will improve upon the safety of our students living in the community, trying to get to Gildo Rey Elementary and Mt. Baker Middle Schools.  Since I've been living at 1401 37th Street SE, I've lost count of the number of students walking in the middle of 37th Street SE, during the Fall - in the early AM and mid PM hours.  During these times, I've witnessed students jumping out of the road, into shrubbery, trying to keep safe from cars speeding up and down the road.  In some cases, 37th Street SE, has literally become a raceway.  

I've also observed families walking with strollers, trying to get to park paths/playgrounds in our neighborhoods.  Just adding a sidewalk, with a cross walk on O street SE, will reduce the risk of pedestrians being hit by cars; and will serve as a profound connection in our neighborhood with the parks, schools, and major bust stops located M Street SE.  

There's even a disabled woman (Dianne), whose disability is blindness, who walks the 37th Street SE path 3 times a week in the early afternoon/evenings for exercise.  She's uses her cane to help guide her way through - trying to avoid the cars speeding up and down 37th Street SE, as well as mailboxes and parked cars on the side of the street. 

Adding a sidewalk on 37th Street SE not only will reduce the risk associated with pedestrians, but it will also make our neighborhood more vibrant, enhance the sense of place, and will improve our city's brand and identity...one more step at a time.  

Please evaluate this request with the intent to act fast and construct a sidewalk on 37th Street SE, beginning at M Street SE - heading towards Olympic Street SE.  If you need me to submit the signatures I've gathered, I will.  

Thank you for your time and consideration
Resident of 1401 37th Street SE - The Family of Simeon P. Rhoden

text: The shoulder of the section of SE 284th street that encompasses the "S" turns is badly in need of grading. The ditch on the north side needs to be pulled and the shoulder shaped and graded.  More crushed rock may need to be added because most of it has washed down the side of the street and off the shoulder.  Even though the speed limit on this street is 25 mph, much of the traffic regularly travels 40 to 50 miles per hour. A pedestrian trying to negotiate this section places his/her live in danger due to the unmaintained, narrow shoulder, and the water runoff uses the street surface rather than the ditch to reach the seasonal stream at the bottom of the hill.  Speed bumps along this street would be the ideal solution, but short of that this "S" turn needs regular shoulder work to keep it safe and to promote good drainage.

text: Almost a year ago, back in February 2019 I asked about why semi trucks were using H Street NW to get to areas North of Main Street and why the no truck traffic signs were removed. I was told it was the most direct route for trucks to get to and from the industrial area on the North side of 2nd Street NW. Was also informed that due to the signs being on H Street NW trucks were instead using the small residential streets to the East. I understand and agree that that wasn’t the proper spot for them. I am beginning to see huge issues with the trucks using H Street as well. The power pole at the corner of 2nd Street NW and H Street NW was damaged so bad by a semi turning right from H Street NW onto 2nd that it had to be removed and replaced. The fire hydrant across the street was ran over and damaged by a truck. Several times I have seen them turn left from 2nd Street NW onto H Street NW, be unable to make the turn onto H Street NW and instead went into the dirt area between the fire hydrant and the train tracks to make the turn. There are huge ruts over there now where one got stuck. Today I came home from work and noticed that the new power pole has been hit and the street sign flattened by a truck turning right onto 2nd Street NW from H Street NW. Something has got to change before it’s our cars, homes or even worse our children who are getting hit.

text:
Over the weekend, a city contractor (Asplundh) completed some very major and very poor pruning on city property. These trees are part of the master plan for the Power District. They are nowhere near power lines, and this cannot be justified by "utility clearance". The city codes require pruning in accordance with ANSI A300 standards. The standards clearly specify that no more than 25% of a tree's canopy may be removed at one time, and that lion's tailing is unacceptable. More than 40-50% of the tree canopies on this property were removed - well over the allowable amount. Further, all lateral branches were removed from these canopies - this is lion's tailing. Not only is this prohibited by ANSI standards, but it truly makes these trees more likely to fail in heavy winds or flooding. ANSI standards also specify how a cut should be made - outside of the branch bark collar bisecting the angle between the branch bark ridge and a line perpendicular to the branch. There are numerous tears, stub cuts, and flush cuts - all of which may lead to increased susceptibility to disease and pests. Many of the residents of the up and coming Power District are absolutely appalled at what is happening to the trees on this property and other surrounding properties owned by GRU, and we ask that you hold yourselves accountable to the same standards you impose on your residents. label: Traffic_Signals_Signs
text:
To be clear, this sign is not obscured/overgrown, but there was not an option for unnecessary or dangerous, so I chose obscured/overgrown.

There is a four-way stop at this very low traffic intersection.  If you are heading south on NW 3rd street from NW 8th Ave, there is also a stop sign at NW 2nd Ave and the stop light at University Avenue.  Essentially, if you are going south, you will stop three time in two blocks.  Given the low traffic at this intersection, it seems unnecessary to have traffic in both directions come to a stop.  This may even be a good place for a roundabout, given the amount of traffic at the intersection.  At least, consideration should be given to only have traffic stop in one direction.

The decision to change the intersection at NW 3rd Street and NW 2nd Avenue from a four-way stop to only stopping in the south direction of NW 3rd Street seems crazy especially given the lack of visibility at this intersection and the designation of NW 2nd Ave as a "bike corridor".  It is very hard for motorists or people on bikes heading down 3rd St to see traffic approaching this intersection on NW 2nd Ave.

text: The pedestrian crosswalk at the bus stop by the Publix on Main street in the center of Main has a zig zag pattern for people to cross. There should be flashing crossing signs provided alerting motorists of pedestrians who want to cross, like there is near NE Boulevard and NE 8th Avenue - a corner with significantly less traffic and no bus stop associated with it.  Please fix this unsafe and cruel hazard as soon as possible!

text:
The Commission received the attached letter via e-mail on Sun., 3/19, 8:21pm:

March 18,2017
Gainesville City Commissioners: Mayor Lauren Poe, Helen Warren, Harvey Budd, Charles Goston, Todd Chase, Craig Carter, Adrian Santos

Greetings,
I want to take this opportunity to address the commission via letter about a few concerns. On March 17, 2017, I attended my grandson’s basketball game at the boy’s club on 2700 N W 51st Street. As I watched the game I was struck by the number of safety hazards and violations our youth were exposed to.
The following violations need immediate attention:
•	Exposed iron beams without protective padding (west center beam) to soften the blow should a child collide upon impact.
•	Much of the concrete interior walls have no protective covering.
•	Poor lighting at the front entrance is acutely inadequate.
•	Vehicles passing in the area are speeding through when children are existing the building and crossing the street.
•	Street lighting in front of the Boys Club poses threats to walking pedestrians.
My request for correction includes the following recommendations:
•	Install paddings for beams and block wall.
•	Increase lighting at front of building and perimeter.
•	Install blinking caution lights approximately 150 yards in front of Club to slow down traffic.
•	Increase street lighting.
I entrust the commission will recognize the urgency of this matter and make the appropriate decisions to correct these flawed conditions. I want to thank you in advance for your indulgence in this matter and I look forward to seeing the changes.
 As you know, our youth are our number one priority. We trust in your leadership to minimize these dangerous conditions at your earliest time frame.

Philoron A. Wright Sr.

label: Streets_Sidewalks
text:
The Mayor & City Commission received this e-mail:

The Mayor and the Commissioners of Gainesville,

My neighborhood streets were recently repaired for pot holes and rough spots. The streets were solid, smooth and level. This turned out excellent. 

Then  you ruined the streets with slop put down by ASPHALT PAVING SYSTEMS. Now the streets are worse than they were. Some streets around here got real solid smooth asphalt. We got this.

The way it was done was terrible. A layer of gravel and tar was put down without warning and suddenly we couldn’t leave our house or return to them, and then we had to drive on it. A week later came the top coat. Same thing. I was ready to go to work and suddenly there’s wet tar in front of my house. I COULD NOT GO TO WORK. PEOPLE COULD NOT GO HOME. No warning. The crew said “Oh well.” This is inexcusable.  You should have warned people. Everyone I’ve talked to is livid.

Then there is the quality of the job. My street, 46th Place, is bad. 47th Avenue is even worse. But then they did pave it in the rain. Tar and water don’t mix.

It is rough, uneven, and peeling up. Weeds are growing through it already. It looks bad. Cars and trucks – especially the garbage trucks - tore it up. Cars that rode smooth now buzz with vibration. Everyone is commenting on how bad this is now, how bad it will be in a few months or a few years, what it will do to our property values. I can now see what  other streets were paved with this substance. It did not hold up – now they are ruts of gravel. This is my neighborhood’s future.

It is clear what this ASPHALT PAVING SYSTEMS is a bad product and they don’t care about the people who live here. It should not been used on a public street. This product should not be used again.

Has anyone from Public Works come to check the work? Have you asked the people who live on these streets about it?  Is there any quality control or follow up? I think the answers are “No.” 

If you think any of this is acceptable, think again. If you can’t afford to do it right, do not do it wrong. This was wrong. 

John Nowak
3207 NW 46 Place
Gainesville FL 32605
[EMAIL]
[PHONE]

I would like to bring to the attention of the Gainesville City Commissioners, the trash that often accumulates along the south side of State Road 24 between UF Health Shands and the Malcom Randall VA Hospital.

I gather that this area is sort of a “no-man’s” land with jurisdiction shared (or not shared) between the City, the University of Florida/Shands, and the VA.

I often walk from the parking garage near the corner of Gale Lemerand Dr and State Road 24 to my office in the Shands Facilities Administration Building. I am dismayed at the trash along the walking area—especially the medical related trash such as latex gloves and face masks and sadly copious cigarette butts.

Mostly recently it has been less littered, and I did make mention of the problem to someone at Shands—so perhaps some action was taken.

But what I would hope in the long term is that the entities involved would work together to provide regular clean up this area and a cooperative educational program for visitors, patients, and employees.

Because of the prominence of the UF Health Shands medical facility and the regional status of the VA, we have a lot of people from out of town visiting this area, and I would hope that the city, the hospitals, and the local community would take pride in showing visitors a well-kept public corridor.

Thank you.

Eleanor K. Sommer, M.Sc.
Graduate Programs Advisor & Adjunct Lecturer
Center for Arts in Medicine
University of Florida College of the Arts

Gainesville FL 32610

Dear Mr. Arreola,

I am writing you today to see if you can help with a problem in our sub-division.  Several months ago there was an auto accident at the entrance to Monterey at NW 34th Place and NW 43rd Street.  A vehicle went off the road and struck and damaged the sign for Monterey.  The driver of the car that damaged the sign was insured with Progressive Select Insurance Company. Monterey sub-division does not have an active Home Owners Association that is responsible for the common areas of the development and therefore does not have an insurable interest in the sign.

It is true that we no longer have an HOA for this development. I am asking you for so assistance to see what can be done to repair the sign without any cost to the homeowners of Monterey or The City of Gainesville.  Maybe if the City Attorney were to talk to the adjuster from Progressive there could be a solution to this problem.

I know that the State of Florida requires all owners/operators of a motor vehicle to have Property Damage insurance of at least $10,000.  The State also requires the motor vehicle owner to pay for damage done to the property of others due to an automobile accident.  The problem here seems to revolve around just who owns the sign and has the insurable interest.

Please let me know if there is someway the City of Gainesville can help us get the sign repaired.  The homeowners have maintained the entrance planters and kept the sign painted for many years.  All we are asking is that the sign be repaired.

The City Commission received the following e-mail this morning (9/7, 9:14am):


To whom it may concern,

My name is Elizabeth DiVito and I live with my boyfriend, Scott Miller, at 432 NW 9th Street. We moved in to this house 5 weeks ago on August 7 and this is my fifth year and Scott's fourth year living in Gainesville in various spots around the city. We have always been impressed by the municipal service the city provides, but we are now realizing that the quality of these services may depend on the relative income level of the neighborhood.

Out of the past five weeks, our garbage has been picked up properly just one time. We have called the city's Solid Waste Division each of those Thursday mornings (our pickup day is Wednesday) and it has still not been made clear to us why the truck continues to miss our street. We are starting to feel like the City of Gainesville is not properly providing municipal services to all of its residents equally. Our neighborhood is mainly old, low-income houses and it seems like the maintenance and cleanliness here is less important than in other areas of the city. We, of course, hope this is not true, but we cannot understand why a municipality would leave garbage uncollected around its neighborhoods. 

Please let us know if there is anything we can do to help alleviate this problem. We would simply like to see this neighborhood reflect the same high standards as the rest of the city.

Thank you in advance for your time and we look forward to hearing from you soon.

Best, 
Elizabeth DiVito
[EMAIL]

text:
Hello,

I'm a life-long Gainesville resident and am on faculty at UF. I'm sorry to bother you, I tried calling earlier today and discovered your office was closed for the storm. I respect you're busy with storm preparations, as am I, and hope all is going well for you & your families.

I'm reaching out to you as I'm very concerned about the construction on NE 6th Avenue between 1st and 5th Streets.
My home is at 305 NE 6th Avenue, I've lived upstairs since 2003 and my father moved in to the downstairs in 2014, he passed away in April from cancer, so I now own both units and am hosting guests evacuating from Miami, in his home, for the storm.

For the past 2-3 months there has been construction on NE 6th Ave between 1st - 5th Streets.
The road was just paved a few days ago and it appears the gutters & curbs are under construction.
I fear that during the storm, in the sections that remain unfinished, the dirt will erode and the entire area will flood.
However, I'm most afraid of the 8 barricades (they look like this: http://www.bobsbarricades.com/bimages/products/barracade1.jpg) currently installed along the north & west sides of NE 6th Ave in the 300 block (immediately in front of my home, built in 1912).

Officials have repeatedly warned that any unsecured objects may become airborne and act as projectiles, shattering windows, etc.
My home is 103 years old and all of the windows are original and impossible to replace (the lovely warped glass). Earlier today I spent two hours moving everything in our yard that's not buried/secured, into the garage-- the porch furniture, potted plants, hoses, our mailbox, trash & recycling bins, etc., as I'm doing the best I can to prevent storm damage.  Can someone please insure me that those barricades will all be removed prior to Sunday?

Ideally, I'd love to hear that the gutters and curbs will also be completed before the rain begins as the lack of concrete in those areas is likely going to cause water to erode the dirt, pool, and flood-- impacting my yard & home and the Thomas Center south-side parking lot.

With much appreciation & respect,
:)

The City Commission & City Manager received the following e-mail today at 12:16pm:

Mr. Mayor,

I signed up for the Town Hall but the forum ran out of time before getting to me.
So here's what I sent to Phil Mann, followed by Phil's response to me.
________________________________________

To: Phil Mann, Public Works
From: Harold Saive
1716 NW 10th Terrace
[PHONE]
RE: Request timeline for action to remedy flooding on 10th Terrace
Flooding Currently  Too High For Normal Automobile Traffic, including, grocery store, medical appointments and prescription med refills.
Flooding has failed to recede after 2 days due to non-functioning City drains at NW 16th Ave and 10th Terrace.
(Speaking on behalf of 10th Terrace neighbors)
Neighbors report their automobiles and transportation by foot are Marooned due to high water.  Only High clearance vehicles can navigate 10th Terrace.
It appears the enormous demand on the City sewer system during IRMA may have caused these drains to reverse flow , accelerating flooding on 10th Terrace beyond that of rainfall from IRMA.
With barely 2 inches of receding waters thus far, these storm drains continue without noticeable flood relief on 10th Terrace with 6-8 inches of standing water in front and back yards as of 10 AM today. 
Wildlife and snakes have been observed by at least 2 neighbors.
Flooding of home interiors and carpeting has been reported, but remediation of mold issues cannot begin until contracted service vehicles can navigate 10th terrace without flooding hazard.
One neighbor was told that 10th Terrace residents are cut off from all services, trash pickup and USPS mail.  They wonder if this includes emergency calls to 911 and EMT response.
Please advise a timeline of relief for 10th terrace  residents.
Thanks, Harold
________________________________________

Mr. Saive:
Unfortunately, due to the extent of the down trees and extensive flooding, our crews have many requests for service holding.  The entire staff has been working almost non-stop since the winds subsided enough to begin response and recovery efforts.
If this request is not already in the system, staff will enter the request in CityWorks and the management team will work to get one of the crews assigned to this task.  We cannot give you an exact timeline as to when this street will be addressed.
Someone from our office will be reaching out to you when they have an idea.
As a suggestion for the future, you can also enter these requests directly into the 311GNV app and they get sent directly to the appropriate Department and staff person to ensure that it gets a response.
Please let us know if you have any additional questions or comments.
Sincerely,
Philip R. Mann, P.E. 
Interim Public Works Director 
City of Gainesville - Public Works Department 
[PHONE] – Office

It is *not* supposed to be a retention pond - and historically, it has never filled up - in fact the survey maps have it listed as "Raintree Park".

The whole block still smells like rancid old gasoline, lawns that were flooded only briefly are dead, and an untold amount went back into the creek. It's the first property near the creek, in the flood zone, and it's likely that the tank is now full of a mixture of old gas and flood water. Even if we don't get another flood in the near future, that tank is going to rust out and drop the remaining fuel.

I wrote on this website a few minutes ago and tried to submit the information. Somehow the description was deleted. I will try again -- hope this is not a duplicate.

During Hurricane Irma three large trees fell from my neighbor's property at 1114 NE 6th Street onto their property and my property. The trees that fell on my property were cleaned-up on September 25th, and the debris was subsequently picked up by the city.

Someone connected with 1114 NE 6th Street eventually hired a tree service to clean up that property. One of the other neighbors told me within the last couple of week that the company cannot complete the job; no one seems to have been working over there for quite a while.

I would like to have my fence repaired and my property maintained appropriately; the fence cannot be repaired until the neighbor's property is cleaned up --at least on the south side of their property's back yard. However, separate from the fence repair, I am also concerned about the amount of debris that keeps sitting on the property of an unoccupied and damaged house -- especially when no one around here seems to know who is "in charge" of the house and property at this time.

I would like my request to be anonymous. I do not want to risk having uncomfortable situation.

There is a dirt parking lot behind these 3 houses that fits 15 cars, however it's always submerged under inches of water. The parking lot has large craters all over that allow rain water to accumulate and sit for days on end. Our cars are parked in inches of standing water, and we frequently have to take our shoes off just to keep them from getting wet when walking to or from our vehicles. Additionally, these craters are so deep that black cables are exposed and floating when submerged in water. This presents a considerable safety concern for 15 students consistently entering and leaving the parking lot on scooters throughout the day.
We tried talking to our property managers about this issue because we should not have to wade to our front door in water. However, they refused to fix the issue. 
What are our options for getting the property managers to remedy this inconvenient and potentially dangerous drainage issue?
Any information is greatly appreciated!

text:
SW 23rd Terrace is a 3-lane road which contains many bus stops. Around 9am and 5pm, this road gets incredibly backed up with traffic, making it difficult to use. I believe this traffic is due to new signs that say "no passing", and an increase in ticketing for passing stopped buses that are loading and unloading on this street. This street is otherwise legal for cars to pass on.

The intent of this "no passing" sign was to make this street safer for pedestrians to cross the road (to get to the many bus stops). This traffic makes it even more dangerous to cross this street as a pedestrian, and is frustrating for drivers, so I believe these signs are actually doing the opposite of what they were intended to do. They are also especially confusing for drivers, given that this street seems like it would be legal to pass on, and the signs are only at the start and end of this road, and most drivers use this road for neighborhood access, and thus do not always see the signs. It would be more beneficial to take these signs down, and instead implement cross walks, or a pedestrian bridge.

Mr. Jeff Look

Mr. Look,

The following e-mail was sent to the City Commission on 6/24, 5:07pm by Beth Murphy ([EMAIL]):

Good Afternoon Mayor Poe and Commissioners,
I wrote in approximately 2 weeks ago about this same issue.  
In taking a bike ride through downtown today, toward Depot Park, I encountered the same trash accumulation I reported on 2 weeks ago outside the now closed Sweet Mel’s Restaurant. If this were public property, certainly the City would put our taxpayer dollars to work to clean the area.  The fact that it is privately owned posses a different issue.  Please, take action.  Please take a walk, make a call…

Is this what we want for Gainesville?  Is this the picture we want for our "New American City" ad??


Concerned Citizen,
Beth Murphy

Mayor Poe received the following e-mail from Brendan Ebersole ([EMAIL]):

Hello Mr Mayor

            I live in downtown Gainesville and I have noticed a disturbing practice in regards to the trash receptacles. In particular the trash can on the north east corner of the Hippodrome, one farther east next to the sun center by the road and another across from the Union Street Station next to the empty lot.

I believe better maintenance of these receptacles would greatly improve the esthetics of the downtown. They could use a good pressure washing too. Maybe it is all of the trash bins downtown that are being neglected but these I walk by most days.

Many times the unsightly privacy fence is open exposing filthy dumpsters. There is frequently loose trash on the ground in the parking lot that this dumpster pit resides. It smells horrid and pungent. I believe a better less prominent location could be found for what I believe is mostly food waste from restaurants. I live next to the Sun Center and the dumpster in their parking lot constantly has trash and broken glass in front of it and smells like wet, pungent neglect. If you look at the back of the dumpsters you will see the dumpsters fluid spill way that drains into the road onto what I believe is 4th ave, the road that goes by GRU. 
            Thank you so much for considering remedies to these issues, I feel it will greatly improve the feel of our beautiful downtown. 

Brendan

-----Original Message-----
From: Jan Frentzen [mailto:[EMAIL]] 
Sent: Thursday, October 18, 2018 8:10 PM
To: citycomm
Subject: Central Builder Supply move

Commissioners -

I am not a City resident, but a long time resident of the county and owner of a business which performs building services within the city,county, and region. I don't know if you are aware of what I am about to describe, but if so, have you considered the consequences?

It has come to my attention that Central Builders Supply - a business with which I have had an account for almost 40 years - is moving from their present location at the NE corner of NW 23rd Ave and 6th Street. Apparently, actions by codes enforcement would impose costs on them 
which they cannot justify - they rent the property from ABC Liquor/Lounge - and so they will close their doors at the end of October and relocate in a facility much less favorable to them and, one would imagine, to the City. The building they will be leaving had been vacant and derelict for several years before they took it over and their presence has been good for the neighborhood and them - they have a very active walk-in business, something they previously lacked at their old location on SR 121. The odds are good that the space will become derelict again and the move may result in CBS ultimately permanently closing their doors.

CBS is a long time locally family owned business with local employees. text:
Currently NW 55th Blvd is clean due to private citizens doing a clean-up. But it is a pervasive problem that the property owners should take care of.  The next road on NW 55th Ave. is currently terribly littered.

"I live in an apartment complex on NW 55th Blvd and the amount of litter people toss out of their cars daily is astounding. It is a curvy road with no sidewalks, in a wooded area, with two gas stations nearby. It is my understanding that this street is not managed by the City of Gainesville and it is not managed by Alachua County (although the EPA does drive by to check Hogtown Creek). Public Works does not mow or remove the litter. I’m told the street is privately owned, but only Creekwood Apts (where I live) picks up litter in front of their property. So, is there a way to contact the street owner? Particularly Palmetto Crerk and Palmetto Walk, which both have copious Litter along their entrances, in the woods. Is this a code violation? I’d like to discuss whether I am allowed to put up signage to encourage folks to keep NW 55th Blvd street clean. See my Instagram account #LitterFreeGNV to view some of the litter I’ve picked up there in only a few months. I find diapers, syringes, and drug baggies regularly, and we live near the creek! . It is relentless. People dump tires and all kinds of other stuff in the forest and on roadsides, as well. We need a litter education campaign in Gville that goes beyond the annual Great American Clean-up. That event is great, but it’s not enough... I see litter all over Gville and it saddens me. I’m sure the plastic bag and styrofoam ban will help; but a bottle deposit would also help; I find tons of recyclables, too. I’d like to discuss how you can help me help my neighborhood."

With the fencing off of the large vacant lot across University for construction, illegal parking of trucks and buses has become more frequent. Like noise it's a low priority, and each vehicle isn't there for long. Would it be possible to get increased parking enforcement patrols there during breakfast and lunch for a little while to at least warn the repeat offenders and help alleviate the problem? "

text: The Thornebrook/Arby's sign at the SE corner of NW 43rd ST and NW 25th PL is an illegal "electronic sign" that is prohibited in Gainesville by Section 30-9.3 of the Code of Ordinances. The prohibition of "electronic signs" has been in place since Ord # 070890 was adopted in April 2008. This sign was installed after that date, so it is not a "legally nonconforming sign". Even if it was a "legally nonconforming sign", Section 30-9.9D. requires the sign to be brought up to code when: 1) sign renovation cost exceeds 50% of sign replacement cost, OR 2) when principal structure on parcel(s) is demolished or renovated at a cost exceeding 50% of assessed value of sign structure, OR 3) the sign is moved for any reason.  IOW, even if the sign was installed prior to 2008 and is therefore a "legally nonconforming sign", the recent renovations to the site and sign because of the Arby's construction mandates that, per code, the sign shall be brought into compliance with Gainesville's sign code.
