text:
Unsecured swimming pool (no locks nor latches on gates) at 2138 NW 29th Place, Gainesville, FL is dangerous for small children in the neighborhood.
  =================  
This is a 2 story white building with a pool in the backyard.  The pool is surrounded by a chain link fence.  This fence has 2 gates, which are usually left open, and are not capable of being secured.  The gates do not have any lock or latch to prevent them being opened from outside.
  =================  
This is dangerous.  It's a big deep pool of water that someone can drown in.  It's easy to get at since the gates to the pool are left open at all times.
  =================  
I have small children.  The pool is visible through the chain link fence from public areas (visible from near the street).  My kids have tried to get at the pool when I've taken them on walks in the neighborhood.
  =================  
2138 NW 29th Place is posted as an Air BnB rental and on numerous other short term rental sites. https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/38580304 https://www.vrbo.com/1803500 https://www.homeaway.com/vacation-rental/p1803500vb https://www.stayz.com.au/holiday-rental/p1803500vb  The owner lives in California.  I have tried contacting the owner by leaving a video voice message on the Ring doorbell, which is an electronic doorbell and security system to where I can knock on the door and the Ring doorbell will record a video and send it to the owner's phone.  I have tried contacting the owner by messaging through the online hotel sites.  I attempted to text the owner, but am not sure whether or not I have his correct phone number.
  =================  
The property is managed by realtor Tammy Broxson.  Tammy Broxson messaged me back through the online hotel rental site Vrbo and stated, "Please be aware there is no requirement to have a padlock on the gate/fence. It is trespassing to enter the property without permission. Any padlocks installed with be removed and the property authorities. Best, Tammy Broxson"
  =================  
Essentially, the realtor who is managing the rental for the owner has stated that she has no intention of securing the gate with any lock or latch.  In response to a description of my 4 year old trying to get at the pool she stated that that's trespassing.  (A small child can't trespass.)  The property manager won't put a lock or latch on the gate and won't secure the pool.
  =================  
Florida Statutes section 515.29 requires pools to be fenced and have a latch or lock on any gates which can't be operated from outside the gate by children.  That law is here http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0500-0599/0515/0515.html .  Florida Statutes, section 515.29(3) states, "Gates that provide access to swimming pools must open outward away from the pool and be self-closing and equipped with a self-latching locking device, the release mechanism of which must be located on the pool side of the gate and so placed that it cannot be reached by a young child over the top or through any opening or gap."
  =================  
Code enforcement can enforce this Florida law requiring a pool to be fenced and the gate to have a lock or latch that cannot be opened from the outside by children.  The state law is referenced in Gainesville city code Sec. 13-191, "In addition to pool safety standards stated in law and rule, the following shall apply: (1) It shall be unlawful for an owner or occupant to create, maintain, keep or allow the existence of any hazardous condition, equipment, facility or fixture associated with a swimming pool, wading pool or hot tub. Failure to comply with this section shall be a major violation."
  =================  
I don't care if you post my information online, and I checked the box to post my info.  I'm not a snitch.  I've gone (tried to go) direct to the owner first through several channels.  A combination padlock costs less than 10 dollars.  For less than 20 dollars, they could make this safe.  Instead the official written position of realtor Tammy Broxson acting on owner John Fulford's behalf is that if a 4 year old drowns in a pool that's "trespassing to enter the property without permission". label: Property_Housing_Code
text:
The house at 2138 NW 29th Place has an unsecured swimming pool.  I live nearby.  I have small children, and they sometimes try to get in the pool.  They can't swim.  2138 is a whole house vacation rental posted to AirBnB, VRBO, and HomeAway, which is intermittently vacant and intermittently occupied by people who have rented the house like a hotel and are there only briefly. The owner lives in California and does not respond to text messages.  The property manager for the vacation rental, Tammy Broxson, has stated that my 4 year old son is trespassing when he's run into the yard and through the gate to the edge of the swimming pool to try and get in the pool, that she is not required to secure the pool, and that she will not secure the pool.
=================
I reported the unsecured pool to code enforcement in December 2019.  At that time, the gates were hanging open.  Code Enforcement left a note on the door.  Now the gates are closed, and there is a lock on each gate.  For the gate on the west side of the house, the gate and fence post are so far apart that I can walk up and pull lightly on the gate and it opens.  So, even though the gate is closed, it's very easy to open it by pushing or pulling and someone doesn't even have to lift the latch to get in.
=================
I, or a child, or anyone else can see the swimming pool from the street, walk up to the gate on the west side of the house, pull it open, and walk up to the edge of the pool.
=================
The swimming pool is a life threatening hazard, because it's deep water that someone can drown in.  The swimming pool needs to be secured.
=================
I attached a photo showing that the gate easily swings open and closed even with a padlock on the fork latch.
=================
Florida Statutes section 515.29 requires pools to be fenced and have a latch or lock on any gates which can't be operated from outside the gate by children. That law is here http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm? App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=05000599/0515/0515.html . Florida Statutes, section 515.29(3) states, "Gates that provide access to swimming pools must open outward away from the pool and be selfclosing and equipped with a self-latching locking device, the release mechanism of which must be located on the pool side of the gate and so placed that it cannot be reached by a young child over the top or through any opening or gap."
=================
Florida Building Code section 424.2.17.1.2 describes requirements for residential swimming pool fencing: "The barrier may not have any gaps, open-ings,  indentations,  protrusions,  or  structural  compo-nents that could allow a young child to crawl under,squeeze through, or climb over the barrier as hereindescribed below. One end of a removable child barriershall not be removable without the aid of tools. Open-ings in any barrier shall not allow passage of a 4-inchdiameter (102 mm) sphere."
=================
Code enforcement can enforce this Florida law requiring a pool to be fenced and the gate to have a lock or latch that cannot be opened from the outside by children. The state law is referenced in Gainesville city code Sec. 13191, "In addition to pool safety standards stated in law and rule, the following shall apply: (1) It shall be unlawful for an owner or occupant to create, maintain, keep or allow the existence of any hazardous condition, equipment, facility or fixture associated with a swimming pool, wading pool or hot tub. Failure to comply with this section shall be a major violation."
=================
Code Enforcement declared this compliant with code in CE-18-00468 and CE-19-03359.  That's not true. It's not compliant to have a situation where someone can easily walk from the street into a swimming pool and drown.
=================
A swimming pool gate which can be pushed or pulled open with light pressure is not compliant because it can be opened from the outside by a small child.  That's not safe.

text:
To whom it may concern, 

Hello. I am currently a resident living in a tent at Dignity Village, and I would like to make a request concerning a recent change in waste management. 

My tent is located in the first section of the southwest corner at Grace Marketplace. There is a road that circles around Grace, and as you are heading south on the road, just before you turn the corner to go east, there is a designated area at the edge of the lot, which contains 3 porta-potties and a cube shaped dumpster with two lids. Both the porta-potties and the dumpster are situated a minimum of 50-60 ft away from any tents. Or, you might say - none of the residents have chosen to set up their tents within 50-60 ft of the designated bathroom and dumpster area. This seems to be a sufficient distance for everyone. However, on Friday morning, January 31st, the dumpster was removed, and a large rectangular dumpster with no lids was placed right in the middle of the main tent area, within 15-20 ft of several of the tents, including my own. 

Although I do not contribute to this myself, it is an unfortunate truth of this type of living environment that the dumpsters will tend to contain urine, feces, and other raw waste, such as old meat. Because of its close vicinity, and because it does not have any lids, I am able to smell the waste from my tent, and there are flies whenever I walk outside my door.

In addition to this, it causes an excess of noise, which has made it difficult for me to sleep at night. When the dumpster is moved from 60 ft away (where it was) to 15ft away (where it is now), it may appear to be a subtle difference to an outsider, but it causes a sound increase of 12db, which more than doubles the perceived volume. Whenever anything is thrown into the dumpster, it usually creates a loud thud sound, which I can not only hear, but I can feel as well, as it shakes the ground. 

I do understand that living in a tent, I am not in a position to expect the same standards as someone living in a house or an apartment, but I would like to respectfully request that the dumpster be moved to its previous position, or to another suitable position that would be located 50 or more feet from any of the tents. And preferably I believe it ought to be the kind of dumpster with lids, so that the flies and smell may be better contained. 

In regards to sound, I do not expect total quiet, and accordingly, I wear earphones literally 24hrs/day. Under normal conditions, the headphones are sufficient for blocking all or most of the sound from the surrounding area. But with the dumpster in its new location, I am able to hear trash being thrown several times per hour, and as I said, this occurs after 10pm at night as well.

Another problem is that the dumpster tends to create debris, and attract scavengers. For example, currently there is a heap of scrap tent materials between the dumpster and my tent. The accepted etiquette here is for anything which may potentially be of use to be left outside the dumpster. Additionally, there are people who regularly check the dumpster for these types of things, and there are also people who regularly go into the dumpster itself in order to retrieve aluminum cans and other items. 

Since the dumpster has been placed in its current position, it has been extremely disturbing for me. If it is possible to move the dumpster to where it was previously, and to return to the type with lids, I would be very grateful for your concern. 

Thank you. 

David Cole Arnold

text:
I am writing in order to submit a request on behalf of all the residents who will soon be moving into the new platform tents at Grace Marketplace. This is regarding the noise caused by low flying aircraft. 

Currently at Dignity Village, because the tents are spaced out over a large area, it is not realistic to expect aircraft to be able to avoid flying directly over a certain number of tents throughout the day. This is understandable given the close proximity to the airport. However, Dignity Village will soon be closing in April, and these same residents are in the process of moving into the new platform tents that are stationed inside of Grace Marketplace. Once this move is complete, all of the tents at Grace Marketplace will be arranged in a fixed precise manner along the back fence line, such that 100+ residents will be located within approximately a 400 ft x 400 ft area. Because of this, we would respectfully request that low flying airplanes be asked to maintain a certain distance away from the tents. We are writing to the City of Gainesville in hopes that you may speak with airport officials on behalf of the residents in making this request. 

The ongoing project goal at Grace Marketplace is to obtain long term sustainable housing solutions for each of the 100+ residents involved. In order to achieve this, every resident is expected to do everything in their power in terms of submitting applications, conducting interviews, and maintaining regular contact with case managers. Ideally these things are best done from inside of the tents, where convenience, comfort, and privacy are maximized. Additionally, some residents may be working online from their tents, and/or receiving healthcare through online telehealth portals. If these residents are under perpetual disturbance, then it may delay the project's ability to achieve success, and it will ultimately end in costing taxpayers more money. 

Grace Marketplace is located right at the border of Airport Noise Subzone C, which requires structures to have a minimum noise level reduction of 25db. Given that the walls of the tents are not impervious to sound, we believe that the noise level should instead be mediated by asking aircraft to avoid flying directly over the heads of the residents. Presently the reality is that on some days, up to 100 low flying airplanes will fly within the immediate vicinity of any single tent. When this occurs the noise is so loud that it can be heard very clearly, even while wearing earplugs and/or headphones. In these cases, the person is able to feel the vibration in the ground and in their bones. At times, the aircraft will fly near enough to cast its shadow inside of the person's tent. This type of noise activity will usually begin before 9am, and run continuously, sometimes up until 11pm. It can be said that on March 12th, 2020, this was certainly true. 

It should be noted that the aircraft referred to in this letter are propeller planes only. Passenger jets are very rarely, if ever, close enough to be heard, at least when the person is wearing earplugs. Therefore it should be reasonable that a propeller plane be able to adjust its flight path, such that it does not cause a large disturbance to the residents. It is understandable that the altitude of the aircraft cannot easily be adjusted, due to their proximity to the airport, and so we are asking that they would please be asked to maintain a certain minimum horizontal radius away from the area of tent platforms located along the back of Grace Marketplace. Otherwise the noise will be a perpetual disruption for residents and staff.

We ask that you please consider, while we may temporarily be homeless, we are still human beings, and we are still citizens of Gainesville. If our health and our ability to conduct necessary communications continue to be disturbed on a regular basis, then it negatively affects the welfare of the public, and in turn costs the taxpayers additional money.  

Thank you.

I am respectfully requesting citation be issued for enforcement or penalty.

There is an individual that feeds cats on a neighboring property (1941 NE 17 Drive). This property is abandoned.

The individual feeding the cats has refused to feed the community cats on their own property, at 1926 NE 17th Dr.

There are 4-6 cats that use the abandoned property. They leave dead animals on my property at least once a week (birds, lizards, rodents). I watch them urinate, defecate, and mark territory on my property and another neighbor's property regularly. They often shelter on my property.

I manage my yard as bird and wildlife friendly, which is promoted as a positive benefit to the city and ecosystems, according to programs promoted by IFAS, the City of Gainesville, and Audubon. 

The invasive cats kill and defiles the social and natural elements of the space that has led to a constant and apparent disturbance to myself and others. It adversely affects the quiet enjoyment of my property, as the three of the invasive cats patrol my property throughout the day and night.

The cat food is replenished daily, which has now also attracted crows to regularly share the space with the cats. This adversely affects the quiet enjoyment of my property, as the crows, new to the area this year, now patrol my property in search of additional food.

This is not only unsightly, it is unhealthy. It degrades the social, aesthetic, and economic value of the neighborhood.  This fits the legal definition of "blighted property."

The individual feeding the cats is also trespassing, despite there is no property owner here to enforce the restriction. 

This is a matter of public health, wildlife conservation, neighborhood pride, and city virtue. 

I called animal control and they denied service, claiming this was a matter for Operation Catnip. Operation Catnip spayed/neutered, and returned the cats, only to allow them to continue defiling my private property. 

Can the city please address this issue? This has been ongoing for two years. This is clearly a conflict between Alachua County "community cats" ordinance, and City of Gainesville animal nuisance ordinance.

This would not be an issue of the individual feeding the cats did so on their property, such that the nuisance of the animals occurred strictly on their property.

label: Trees_Vegetation
text:
My wife and I both feel that the ~70-foot dead pine tree rooted at 8465 NW 38th Dr, Gainesville, FL  32653 (owner: Douglas Begin), poses a threat to our home (and ourselves) located at 8480 NW 38th Terr, Gainesville, FL  32653.  The tree in question is rooted approximately 15-feet from our house.  I am not an Arborist, but I am a retired professional engineer (licensed in Ohio).  The tree started dying about 2-years ago and appears to be quite dead at this point.  A healthy pine tree will bend and sway with the forces of the wind.  A dead/dying pine’s fibers harden and become brittle.  A good strong wind/hurricane will cause the tree to snap.  If so, a pine of this size would surely cause irreparable damage to a home and property; not-to-mention the possibility of injury or loss-of-life.
It is one-thing when a storm causes a healthy tree to fall and cause property damage … the law considers this an act-of-god and holds no one truly responsible.
But when an obvious known threat is looming over us … as we feel this pine tree is doing, we feel it would be prudent to act now and have this tree professionally removed.

text: With lesser traffic on the roads, this might be the time to address this issue. For cars coming down the hill on 23rd St and approaching 8th Ave, at the junction, it is very difficult to see the vehicles coming down the hill (i.e. going east to west) due to lack of line of sight. This is particularly hazardous for those vehicles which intend to turn left. The drivers have to inch forward almost into inrushing traffic going west to east to make sure (a) there's no traffic on the left coming from the direction of 34th St and (b) after going quite a bit, then get the visibility of vehicles coming from the direction of 22nd St. The latter vehicles, coming down the hill, are often quite fast. So, the poor driver who's trying to turn left on 8th Ave suddenly finds herself trying to pull away from those cars coming down the hill, and the drivers on those cars then are trying to decelerate in the last second. This is all due to the fact that the cars that are on 23rd St cannot see the cars on 8th Ave (and vice versa) until they have forwarded well into 8th Ave. This is quite dangerous, and there needs to be some sort of a traffic signal at that intersection so that cars coming down the hill on 8th Ave know that they have to slow down in order to allow the cars on 23rd St turn safely right onto 8th Ave.

After tearing up the concrete driveway a couple days ago, they started digging today (we believe without first calling 811 to avoid hitting utility lines – as there were no markings, flags and/or visits from GRU or other entities prior to them beginning work) and broke the gas line against my house with their shovel, causing a gas leak which had to be stopped by the Gainesville Fire Department and repaired by GRU. 
Upon searching for permits issued for this property, I have found none publicly listed. Therefore, I am requesting with urgency that code enforcement review the work being performed at 916 NW 6th avenue (my address) and 920 NW 6th avenue (my neighbors) as the issue has gotten to a point where I don’t feel safe being here as they attempt to go around following the correct protocol and receive proper permitting.
Occurrences during this period of time (mid October to present) include (but are most likely not limited to):
Our landlord constructing a fence in 920 NW 6th avenue’s backyard.
Converting the shed into a residential dwelling.
Tearing up the driveway between 920 and 916 NW 6th avenue
Parking a construction dumpster in our driveway
Attempting to work on sewage pipes (which led to the unintentional rupture of the gas pipe)
I have multiple pictures and videos which show the constructed fence, work being done currently in our driveway, the exposed gas line, the construction dumpster, and ultimately the shed which was converted into an efficiency, and will be happy to provide them if needed.

text:
I am new to the neighborhood - having moved here about a year ago.  I heard about the fire that occurred at 401 SE 6th Terrace about 3 years ago.  I was sorry to hear that a neighbor suffered such a terrible loss.  However, there are some serious problems at the property that can no longer be ignored and are affecting the health, property values, safety and wellbeing of everyone in the neighborhood.  I am also told that some neighbors have observed activity the property late into the evenings and early mornings, and believe that the owner, or worse, somebody other than the owner, may be living on the premises.  

I trust the city will take immediate and real action, and do something about this troubling situation.  Only the City has the authority to make this right, and citizens are forced to live with the results and consequences of the city's actions or inaction.  I have the following:

1.  Is there a valid permit on file with the City for restoration? I haven't seen any work taking place for over a year, and according to my neighbors, no work has taken place for at least two years or more.
2.  The house is in an historic district and has been allowed to become completely dilapidated.  Owners in this district, like other districts around the City are all required to comply with the strict regulations to maintain our properties in accordance with the historic district.  Why is this property permitted to negatively affect the values of surrounding properties?  Why does the City look the other way and refuse to enforce City codes that are so obviously being flouted and ignored?
3.  There are piles of trash and discarded household belongings scattered all over the property, but especially in the backyard where it is piled up to about 6' high.  Rainwater collects in and on the various items, and is causing a potentially serious refuge for diffuse mosquito breeding and proliferation.  These piles of trash are also, without irony, another potential fire hazard to the property and to the adjacent neighbors.
4.  The entire yard is completely overgrown.
5.  At least one, and possibly two unregistered vehicles are on the property, or may be parked - for years - on the city street parking.
6.  A dead animal smell has been detected coming from the garage area where a storage pod is located.
7.  Possums and raccoons have been observed going in and out of the property.
8.  The roof of the garage structure has large holes and appears to be caving in.
9.  The fence is dilapidated and doesn't appear to be structurally sound.  The piles of trash and refuse in the backyard can easily be seen through the fencing from the street.
10.  The storage pod has been in the driveway area for at least a year or more.  Is there any City ordinance regulating how long one of these pods can be kept on a property?
11.  There doesn't appear to be any power at the address.
12.  Is this property abandoned or is someone living there?

This letter is being written on behalf of multiple concerned neighbors and households who feel they deserve to remain anonymous to avoid any backlash or vindictiveness from anybody.  Other neighbors have also reported that previous complaints about this property were unheeded and ignored.  

We demand the City of Gainesville's Code Enforcement immediately look into this dilapidated property for these items listed above.  The City must take any and all necessary and legal action to bring the premises up to code, for the protection of our neighborhood and community.

text:
Bass has been coming into our home for over an hour now and it looks like Swamp City is gearing up for another day....night...and weekend of it. 

Neighbors and a policewoman have said that you have to meet a certain decibel level at 200 feet away, I'm a lot more than 200 feet away and I can hear it through three walls. So can my kids.

As for those decibels the ordinance says something different. 

Section 15.2 says the following is a noise disturbance...read (3) carefully.

" Noise disturbance means any sound which:

(1)

Disturbs a reasonable person of normal sensitivities;

(2)

Exceeds the sound level limits set forth in this chapter; or

(3)

Is plainly audible as defined in this section.

Person means any person, person's firm, association, copartnership, joint venture, corporation, or any entity public or private in nature.

Plainly audible means any sound or noise produced by any source, or reproduced by a radio, tape player, television, CD player, electronic audio equipment, musical instrument, sound amplifier or other mechanical or electronic soundmaking device, or nonamplified human voice that can be clearly heard by a person using his/her normal hearing faculties, at a distance of 200 feet or more from the real property line of the source of the sound or noise. "

There appear to be entries for this address dating back over two years. Is the owner an informant for GPD so he gets a pass to screw families and the neighborhood?  It is hard to believe that as many people as have filled out this form that GPD has never issued a citation.

I know that the staff and the Commission have been talking about parking downtown.  Parking in this town is a big problem, and I am not advocating for it to be free. What we had not anticipated was the SmartPhone app.  That is really confusing—especially when you are watching for Curtain time.

For years I brought bills to place in the machine at 311 S. Main.  I did this, in the rain, on Saturday night.  But it turns out I put them in the wrong machine and didn’t get a receipt.  And then we were towed!  But I paid!  Trying to explain and rectify this has been a maze of doors without people, web sites that don’t give contact information, and an unsympathetic clerk at the towing yard.

I just want to say that the parking issue is VERY confusing.  Every SmartPhone solution causes some older folks to swear they will never again go downtown.

text:
A special event noise permit was granted to an outdoor concert at Flavet Field for March 22, 2023 leading to a nuisance noise event that started during the afternoon of March 22 while they were testing the sound system for over an hour, and continued when the concert started in the evening and went on past 10pm. I believe the permit was issued in error. My understanding of the city noise ordinance is that no permit can be granted for the use of loudspeakers on the exterior of a building. The Flavet Field stage certainly seems to fit the description of loudspeakers attached to the exterior of a building. The concerts at that location should need to be run at noise levels pursuant to the noise levels described in Table II of the ordinance for residential areas (colleges and universities are defined residential in the ordinance). For a weeknight this would be 61dB until 10PM at which point it must be reduced to 55dB. This event clearly was granted an illegitimate permit that interfered with the quiet enjoyment of my property nearly 3/4 of a mile away. Please ensure future permits do not allow for the use of loudspeakers attached to the exterior of the stage building to exceed noise levels prescribed in the ordinance. 

(d) Use of loudspeakers on exterior of building. No permit may be issued to permit the use of any loudspeaker or sound device on the exterior of any building which at any time exceeds the sound level limits in Table II, except those used for emergency systems or devices as allowed by section 15-3(d)(6) above.

text:
The discount tire operation withing the Gator City Motors building on 1700 N Main Street is improperly storing 1500  tires of which are holding rainwater and breeding immense amounts of Aedes albopictus and Aedes aegypti. These mosquitoes are capable of spreading many diseases including Yellow Fever, Dengue, and Zika. 

The business owner, Jason, has been consulted about ordinance requirements and the seriousness of the public health issue these conditions allow, but has made no effort to rectify the situation. In fact, he was notified almost three years ago by a former mosquito control technician, but clearly he has ignored the ordinance and has only expanded the problem.

City of Gainesville Mosquito has treated the area to reduce the mosquito populations the tires are generating, but it is imperative that the mosquito breeding conditions of how these tires are being stored is resolved. The invasive species that the tires are breeding are two of the most important disease vectors and pestiferous mosquitoes in public health. Most of these mosquitoes are feeding off the residents of the nearby Sunshine Park apartments then returning to the tires to lay eggs and continue developing.

Subject: URGENT: Traffic Safety and Enforcement Request – Intersection of Dole St. & Alexander St.

To Whom It May Concern,
I am writing to formally request an immediate traffic safety investigation and increased police enforcement at the intersection of Dole Street and Alexander Street, specifically focusing on the traffic flowing toward the H-1 Freeway on-ramp.

There is a severe, chronic issue with motorists failing to stop at the stop sign on Dole Street. Because this route serves as a major conduit for rental cars exiting Waikiki, a high percentage of these drivers are tourists who are speeding, unfamiliar with the roads, navigating via GPS, and rushing toward the freeway. This combination has caused numerous near-misses and accidents. I request that the City and County of Honolulu review this intersection for the following engineering and enforcement solutions: Enhanced Visual Warnings: Installation of "Stop Ahead" pavement markings, highly visible reflective red strips on the stop sign posts, or a blinking LED stop sign. Targeted Traffic Enforcement: Regular HPD speed traps and stop-sign enforcement during peak afternoon traffic periods. Traffic Calming Measures: Assessment for a raised intersection, prominent crosswalks, or a multi-way stop configuration.  Thank you for your prompt attention to preventing further accidents at this high-risk location.  THANK YOU !!

text:
The traffic sign on Halekauwila Street in Honolulu has been struck by a motor vehicle and has been knocked down. The sign is no longer in place and requires inspection and replacement. This sign informs drivers that left turns into the Ililani Condominium are prohibited. It serves an important role in maintaining safe traffic flow and protecting motorists exiting the Ililani parking garage. This is approximately the second time within the past three months that this sign has been knocked down. Following the previous incident, the City and County installed green and yellow reflective tape on the sign pole to improve its visibility.

I respectfully request that the sign be reinstalled as soon as possible. text:
Aloha,
Thank you for taking the time to review my concerns. I'm requesting assistance with an ongoing health and safety issue affecting my apartment in Wahiawa. A tree from the neighboring Wendy's property extends over the property line and hangs directly above my lanai. Chickens regularly roost in its branches, leaving feathers, droppings, debris, and occasionally rotting eggs beneath the tree. The branches also continually grow into my lanai, requiring frequent trimming. In addition, loud crowing and clucking begin as early as 3:00 a.m. and continue throughout the day, significantly disrupting my family's sleep and well-being. These conditions have created an ongoing sanitation and health concern. Poultry waste and decaying organic matter can release airborne contaminants and attract rodents and flies, while simply trimming the tree allows it to regrow and continue attracting the flock. As a result, the same unsanitary conditions—including droppings, feathers, dander, mold, rotten eggs, and excessive noise—continue to return. If it is only trimmed back, it will simply regrow and continue attracting the roosters and chickens, leading to an ongoing  accumulation of mold, noise, droppings, dander, and rotten eggs. The same unsanitary conditions will continue to return. Over the past five years, my son‘s health has been adversely affected because of these ongoing conditions where he has had to have nasal surgery, and I cannot allow this to continue. Under Hawaii case law (Whitesell v. Houlton and Spittler v. Char), overhanging trees that cause harm or create a nuisance may require corrective action. Because this tree extends into my living space and prevents me from safely using my lanai, I respectfully request that property management work with Wendy's to:
Coordinate the cleanup of accumulated poultry waste and rotting eggs.
Arrange for the complete removal of the tree to permanently eliminate this recurring issue.
I look forward to hearing from you, Mahalo.

Please consider appropriate follow-up by Parks and Recreation, outreach services, and/or other appropriate City personnel to ensure that the restroom remains available and safe for women and children using Puʻuloa Beach Park.

Dear City and County of Honolulu Parks and Recreation Department,

I am requesting a comprehensive assessment and major repair and beautification project for the Kaneohe District Park tennis courts and parking area.

The courts have numerous cracks and deteriorated areas, and sand frequently accumulates on the surface during windy conditions, making the courts slippery and potentially unsafe.

The courts and parking lot also experience water ponding after rain. The parking lot has numerous potholes and deteriorated areas that collect water, creating additional concerns for vehicles and pedestrians.

I request consideration of the following improvements:

* Repair and resurface the tennis courts.
* Improve drainage to prevent ponding and allow faster drying after rain.
* Address recurring sand accumulation.
* Repair/refresh fencing, nets, lines, and surrounding landscaping.
* Add a dedicated tennis practice wall with space for individual players.
* Add separate, dedicated pickleball courts rather than painting pickleball lines over tennis courts.
* Repair and resurface the parking lot, including potholes and drainage.

Kailua District Park Tennis courts provides a good model. Its courts are in better condition and have separate tennis and pickleball courts, a practice wall, and surfaces that drain and dry quickly after rain without significant ponding. Similar improvements at Kaneohe would provide a safer, more functional, and more attractive facility for the community.

Thank you for considering this request and forwarding it to the appropriate department for evaluation.

Sincerely,

Kaneohe Resident

text:
August 10, 2026

Re: Urgent Safety Concern – Faded/Unmarked Red Curb at 234 Ohua Avenue

This notice is being documented regarding an ongoing safety concern in front of 234 Ohua Avenue, Honolulu, Hawaii.

The curbside area in front of the property was previously marked red/no parking; however, the red paint has become severely faded and is now barely visible. As a result, vehicles are frequently parking in this restricted area.

This is creating a significant safety hazard for residents exiting the building’s parking stalls. Because Ohua Avenue is a one-way street, vehicles parked along this area severely obstruct the residents’ view of approaching traffic, creating the potential for a serious vehicle accident.

The obstruction also creates additional safety and access concerns, including interference with emergency access and difficulty for large commercial and delivery trucks attempting to maneuver and back into the delivery/loading area serving the neighboring Banyan property.

We have attempted to contact the appropriate government authorities to have the curb properly repainted and the restriction made clearly visible. At this time, we have not been able to obtain a resolution.

This notice is therefore being maintained as a formal record that the hazardous condition has been identified and that efforts have been made to have the appropriate authorities address it. We are requesting that the curb be inspected and repainted as soon as possible to clearly establish the no-parking area and reduce the risk of an accident, injury, or obstruction of emergency and commercial access.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this public safety concern.

Cesar Soto
Resident Manager
234 Ohua Avenue

Complaint: Mililani Exit 5 Road Conditions

I am submitting a complaint regarding the extreme potholes on Mililani Exit 5 extending from the beginning of the exit ramp all the way to the traffic light.

The condition of this roadway is unacceptable. The potholes are severe enough to cause significant wear and tear on vehicles, including potential damage to tires, wheels, suspension components, and steering systems. Drivers shouldn't have to choose between hitting a pothole or making an unsafe maneuver to avoid one.

Hawaiʻi residents already pay substantial vehicle registration and related fees, with a significant amount of public funding dedicated to transportation and roadway maintenance. Yet the condition of many of our roads continues to result in unnecessary and expensive vehicle repairs for residents.

It is extremely frustrating to have to spend additional money maintaining and repairing our vehicles because of inadequate road maintenance. At times, driving on Oʻahu's roads genuinely feels like driving in a developing country rather than one of the most expensive states in the United States.

I also question why the State continues to use road materials and repair methods that appear to deteriorate so quickly. Given the amount residents pay in taxes, registration fees, and other transportation-related costs, I believe Hawaiʻi should be investing in higher quality materials and more durable road construction methods that provide better longevity and reduce the constant cycle of patching and deterioration.

Please inspect Mililani Exit 5 and address these potholes as soon as possible. More importantly, I would like to see a long-term solution rather than another temporary patch that will deteriorate again within months.

⚠️ WELCOME TO THE MEHEULA PARKWAY LAUNCH PAD
Proceed at your own risk.

I'm sure this started as a tree root doing what tree roots do. But at this point, the tree has apparently decided it wants to participate in traffic engineering. 🌳

text:
**Subject:** Request for Emergency Debris Removal Assistance – Fallen Plumeria Trees from Lala Storm (Fence-Line Impact)

Dear City and County 311 Team,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to respectfully request assistance with the removal of substantial tree debris resulting from the recent Lala storm.

Two mature plumeria trees, each over 30 years old—one on my property and one on my neighbor’s—were destroyed during the storm. Both trees fell across our shared fence lines onto each other’s properties. For safety reasons we were required to cut them down, and we are now left with a significant volume of heavy wood and large branches. Many of these pieces weigh more than I do and are far too heavy for the kupuna in our household to move.

Our green waste bins are already full. Clearing the remaining debris through regular collection would require multiple weeks of successive pickups. We also do not have a working truck available to haul the material ourselves.

I kindly ask that a debris-removal truck be dispatched to our location. When the crew arrives, would it be possible for the driver to allow us to fill additional bins or load extra material while they are on site? This would greatly help us complete the cleanup efficiently and safely.

I understand many residents are facing similar challenges after the storm, and I appreciate the City and County’s ongoing efforts to support the community during recovery.

I have attached a photograph showing the trees at the time they fell for your reference. Please let me know if any additional information, photos, or an address confirmation is needed. I am happy to coordinate a convenient time for the crew’s visit.

Thank you very much for your time, consideration, and assistance. Mahalo.

Sincerely l,
Shelby Pikachu Billionaire

[EMAIL]

I would like to report a serious safety concern involving the bus driver of Bus 4053, #6 route.

At approximately 12:46 p.m. today, I was traveling on University Avenue and attempting to merge into the right lane in order to turn onto Beretania Street with my young son in the car. I activated my turn signal and had approximately 40 feet of clearance to safely merge. As I was beginning to merge, the bus driver accelerated and deliberately closed the available gap, preventing me from entering the lane.

This was unnecessarily aggressive and dangerous driving. It is especially concerning given current road conditions following yesterday’s hurricane, with traffic signals still out at various locations around Honolulu and drivers needing to exercise additional caution.

A professional bus driver operating a large public transit vehicle should not accelerate to prevent another vehicle from completing an otherwise safe, properly signaled merge. The driver’s actions created a needless risk of a collision.

Please investigate this incident and take appropriate corrective or disciplinary action with respect to the driver of Bus 4053. I would also appreciate confirmation that this complaint has been received and reviewed.

text:
Subject: Request for Inspection and Maintenance of Tall Palm Trees on Alaʻoli Street Median, Foster Village

Location: Alaʻoli Street, Foster Village, Honolulu, HI (main entrance to Foster Village facing Radford High School)

Description of Concern:

Resident Deborah Waters is requesting an inspection of the palm trees located in the center median along Alaʻoli Street, the main entrance into Foster Village. According to the resident, several of the trees appear to be extremely tall, potentially 40 feet or more in height, significantly exceeding the height of nearby homes.

The resident is concerned that the trees may pose a public safety hazard, especially during periods of high winds or severe weather. UBJECT: URGENT SAFETY HAZARD & LIABILITY COMPLAINT: Damaged Median Fencing and Illegal Crossings on North Vineyard Boulevard.  To the City and County of Honolulu Department of Facility Maintenance / Department of Transportation Services:This is a formal, high-priority safety complaint regarding recurring, hazardous pedestrian behavior enabled by severe property damage to City and County infrastructure. Despite prior reports submitted via the Honolulu 311 (Laulima) system, the situation remains unresolved and is escalating in danger.Location of Concern:The median fencing along North Vineyard Boulevard, specifically the stretch between the Liliha Street/Vineyard intersection and the A‘ala Street/Vineyard intersection.Infrastructure Failure:The existing median fencing has been intentionally cut and vandalized in multiple areas. There are now several large holes acting as unauthorized pedestrian walkways. The most severe breach is located directly adjacent to the entrances of Liliha Square and the Kauluwela II complex.Immediate Public Safety & Liability Risks:Vulnerable Pedestrians at Risk: Daily and nightly observations confirm a high volume of pedestrians—including mothers carrying infants, parents pushing strollers, and young, unsupervised children—running across multiple lanes of heavy traffic on Vineyard Boulevard.Bypassing Safe Infrastructure: These individuals are actively bypassing the designated, signalized crosswalks at the Vineyard/Liliha and Vineyard/A‘ala intersections because these fence holes provide an easy, highly dangerous shortcut.Property Access Facilitation: Pedestrians are cutting through the median fence to directly access the Waena Apartments black-gated entrance, creating a predictable, repetitive path of extreme danger.

Immediate Infrastructure Fortification: We request that the City repair the damaged median fence immediately using reinforced, anti-cut, and tamper-resistant materials. The standard chain-link or metal gated type structure.

Individuals and additional visitors come throughout the day and night, frequently blocking our parking gates and access to the alley. We have also observed suspected drug activity, people sleeping under blankets, and individuals urinating into buckets in the alley. The group appears to be growing and can often be found along the wall near the 24th Street BART station. They have attempted to block access to the alley by using barricades. We are requesting assistance from local authorities to address the ongoing activity, clear the alley, and restore safe and unobstructed access for residents and neighboring properties.

text: This parklet (which is NEVER USED by Earthfire Arts -- one time in my two-plus years of living here did I see a birthday party they were hosting occur in this parklet) has become the overnight site once again of several people and their dog. But now they've been there for weeks (only in the evenings, it's not an actual "encampment") and between the trash left behind, occasional fights/issues at night and then today a lot of liquid human excrement in front of our building, we all feel we are done with it. My neighbor spent a long time cleaning it up this morning so that others wouldn't step in it or make a bigger mess. Earthfire Arts needs to take more responsibility or take down the parklet. Because the parklet isn't in front of their own space (it's around the corner from them), whatever goes on there doesn't even impact them and that's unfair to us neighbors who have to live with the impact every day. We've all been asking for this eyesore to be torn down for awhile (it's unsightly, constantly gets graffiti-ed, and most importantly it completely blocks other cars' sight of our driveway so that we've had multiple close calls in cars and bikes.
